newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Mideast strife hits Israeli tourism industry hard.
newsitem.headline: Mideast strife hits Israeli tourism industry hard.

text.p: The Middle East peace crisis is hurting Israel's tourism industry and could lead to a loss of $500 million in revenue this year, the Israeli Hotels Association said on Monday.
Association spokesman Gilad Nachum said he expected 2.1 million tourists to visit Israel this year compared with 2.4 million visitors in 1996.
Projections based on trends in the first part of 1997 showed revenues from tourism will drop $500 million to $3 billion by the end of the year, he said.
Israel's Central Bureau of Statistics reported similar findings.
"It's due to a lack of secure feelings among foreign tourists," Nachum said. "It prevents them from coming in masses to Israel."
A four-year increase in tourism was snapped last year by a series of bus bombings by Moslem militants in which 59 people were killed.
"Then Netanyahu came to power. The peace process with the Arabs is frozen," Nachum said. "Nothing is getting warmer."
Peace would improve tourism but Nachum said a marketing campaign by the Israeli government abroad would also help attract visitors.
He said he hoped the turn of the millennium and Israel's 50th anniversary celebrations next year would bring in more tourists.
"It will help us," he said. "We want more dollars coming into Israel."
